title: Quietest Person at Least as Rich
statement:
There are n people, numbered 0 to n − 1. Each has a distinct quietness score quiet[i]; lower means quieter. You also get facts richer[k] = [a, b], meaning person a has strictly more money than person b. The facts never contradict each other.

Person y is known to be at least as rich as x if y = x, or a chain of facts leads from y down to x (y richer than someone who is richer than … x).

Return an array answer where answer[x] is the quietest person known to be at least as rich as x.

examples.why: For person 0 the candidates are 0, 1 and 2, since 2 → 1 → 0 is a chain. Person 1 is quietest (3).
No facts: each person only knows about themself.
Person 2 has three people above: 0, 1 and, through 0, person 3. Person 3 is quietest. Person 1 has nobody above, so the answer is 1.

constraints: All pairs in richer are distinct and consistent (no cycles)
hints: Draw an arrow from each poorer person to each richer one. The candidates for x are x plus everyone reachable from x along the arrows.
Running a fresh search from every person repeats a lot of work. The answer for x is x itself or the answer for someone directly richer than x.
Memoised DFS: ans[x] starts as x; for each direct richer y, compute ans[y] and keep it if quiet[ans[y]] < quiet[ans[x]].

explain.intuition:
Turn the facts into a graph with an edge from b to a whenever a is richer than b. The people at least as rich as x are exactly x and everything reachable from it. Since the facts are consistent, the graph has no cycles.

A separate search from every node costs O(n · (n + E)). The saving comes from noticing that the set reachable from x is x plus the reachable sets of its direct richer neighbours. So the quietest one in it is x or one of the neighbours' answers. Compute answers with a DFS and cache them, so each node and edge is handled once. It is the same caching you would do when computing a derived value over a component tree.
steps: Build up[b]: the list of people directly richer than b.
solve(x): if cached, return it. Set best = x. For each y in up[x], let c = solve(y); if quiet[c] < quiet[best], set best = c. Cache and return best.
Call solve for every person and return ans.
pitfalls: Looking only at direct facts. In the first example person 2 is above person 0 only through person 1.
Pointing the edges the wrong way and collecting poorer people instead of richer ones.
Forgetting that x itself is a candidate. When nobody is known to be richer, the answer is x.

solutions.title: Search upward from every person
solutions.idea: For each person run a BFS along the richer-than edges and pick the quietest person reached.

solutions.title: Memoised DFS
solutions.idea: ans[x] is x or the best of ans[y] over the people y directly richer than x. Cache each answer so every edge is followed once.

followups: Do it without recursion using a topological order (Kahn's algorithm), richest people first.
Facts arrive one at a time and you must answer queries in between. What can you update incrementally?
